story.title: Conversation history belongs in the safety test
paragraphs: A model that handles an isolated unsafe request appropriately may behave differently when that request appears within a conversation. Earlier turns change the interpretation of later ones, and evaluating only the final message can miss that dependence. DAMON treats conversation as the unit of robustness testing. Its research value lies in measuring whether safety behavior remains reliable as dialogue context accumulates.

The comparison with predefined dialogue patterns is important. A fixed pattern tests one route through a conversation, whereas an adaptive evaluation can expose failures that depend on earlier model responses. At a high level, DAMON uses tree search to organize alternative dialogue trajectories. The assessment has to track both whether a response violates the intended safety boundary and whether it still addresses the original test objective.

mechanism.title: Distinguish harmfulness from task completion
paragraphs: The paper evaluates five model configurations on AdvBench, MaliciousInstruct, and HarmBench, comparing against six prior methods. AdvBench is reduced to 50 representative, nonduplicate instructions. Automated evaluation uses a GPT-4o judge with a five-level harmfulness scale, counting success only at the highest level. These choices define what the reported attack success rate measures; it is a benchmark outcome under a specific adversarial protocol.

Human assessment adds a second check. Three annotators independently evaluate a random sample of 20 HarmBench instances using GPT-4o as the tested model, with majority voting. A response must both contain harmful content rather than a refusal and address the original objective rather than drift to an unrelated topic. This is a small validation set, but the two-part criterion guards against rewarding irrelevant content merely because it contains concerning language.

A separate context experiment re-evaluates generated test messages with no preceding history, unrelated history, or their original history. As an illustrative measurement question, hold the final message fixed and change only what came before it: does the safety judgment change? This comparison helps reveal a dependency that a collection of independent single-turn tests would conceal, without requiring the website to reproduce unsafe prompts or trajectories.

evidence.title: A stress test, not an everyday failure probability
paragraphs: The original conversation context produces substantially more failures than removing it, and unrelated context can also increase failures. The study additionally tests perplexity filtering, paraphrasing, and a moderation guardrail. These defenses reduce success unevenly; none resolves the measured problem across all tested models. Such results support evaluating dialogue-aware defenses, but they do not establish that any one defense is ineffective in every deployment configuration.

The figures are conditional on deliberately adversarial benchmark objectives, tested model versions, search resources, and an automated judge. They cannot be read as the likelihood that an ordinary user conversation causes harm. The authors also acknowledge manually specified objectives and hand-designed strategy families. Their suggestion that a mismatch between pretraining and safety alignment contributes to the vulnerability is a hypothesis, not a causal conclusion established by the experiments. Broader coverage and larger independent human assessments remain necessary.
